question: △ABC and △PQR are respectively congruent. If AB = 8 = PQ, BC = 10 = QR and ∠B = 35º, then what is the value of ∠P + ∠C?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In congruent triangles, corresponding parts are equal. Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, we know that ∠A = ∠P.

The sum of the internal angles in ΔABC is 180º, which gives us ∠A + ∠C = 180º − ∠B.

Substitute ∠A with ∠P directly: ∠P + ∠C = 180º − 35º = 145º.

**∴ The correct answer is 145º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR

AB = PQ = 8 units, BC = QR = 10 units

∠B = 35º

**Concept Used:**

If two triangles are congruent, their corresponding parts are equal (CPCTC).

The sum of angles in a triangle is exactly 180º.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, the corresponding angles map to each other in exactly the same order.

⇒ ∠A = ∠P, ∠B = ∠Q, and ∠C = ∠R

⇒ In ΔABC, the sum of internal angles equals 180º.

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ Substitute the given value of ∠B = 35º into the equation:

⇒ ∠A + 35º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 180º − 35º

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 145º

⇒ Since ∠A = ∠P, substitute ∠A with ∠P in the equation:

⇒ ∠P + ∠C = 145º

**∴ The correct answer is 145º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruent Triangles (CPCTC)

When two triangles are congruent, all of their corresponding sides and angles are equal. This property is known as Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent (CPCTC).

Angle Sum Property of a Triangle

The sum of all three internal angles of any planar triangle is strictly equal to 180º. i.e., ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º.

Conditions for Congruency

Two triangles can be proven congruent using five standard criteria: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).
